name: Corn Chowder
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Boston crackers well buttered and soaked five minutes in hot water
ingredients.originalText: Six Boston crackers well buttered and soaked five minutes in hot water

ingredients.name: pinch of soda in the milk
ingredients.originalText: A pinch of soda in the milk

instructions.text: Fry the onions in two tablespoonfuls of butter in the soup-kettle
Remove this to the table and take out the onions with a skimmer, leaving the browned butter in the bottom
Put into this a layer of corn cut from the cob, then of crackers, next of sliced parboiled potatoes, seasoning as you go, until all the ingredients are in
Cover with the hot water, and cook gently for about forty minutes after it begins to boil
Heat the milk in a separate vessel, stir into it a tablespoonful of butter rolled in flour, and at last a beaten egg
Pour the milk into the tureen, then the chowder, stirring all the while

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Fry the onions in two tablespoonfuls of butter in the soup-kettle
2. Remove this to the table and take out the onions with a skimmer, leaving the browned butter in the bottom
3. Put into this a layer of corn cut from the cob, then of crackers, next of sliced parboiled potatoes, seasoning as you go, until all the ingredients are in
4. Cover with the hot water, and cook gently for about forty minutes after it begins to boil
5. Heat the milk in a separate vessel, stir into it a tablespoonful of butter rolled in flour, and at last a beaten egg
6. Pour the milk into the tureen, then the chowder, stirring all the while
